findings.title: Experiential Reflective Learning for Self-Improving LLM Agents (ERL)
findings.source: arXiv (March 25, 2026) — published at ICLR 2026 MemAgents Workshop
findings.summary: ERL builds a persistent pool of reusable heuristics extracted from past task trajectories; at test time relevant heuristics are retrieved and injected into context, improving GAIA2 success rate by +7.8% over ReAct baseline without fine-tuning.
findings.relevance_notes: Directly maps to George's dream cycle. George already reflects on past nights and generates improvements — ERL formalizes this as a heuristic pool that is retrievable at task time. A 'heuristics.md' file could be seeded from past failures and successes for injection into future task prompts.

findings.title: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework v0.2.0
findings.summary: Seven-agent trading firm architecture (Fundamentals, Sentiment, News, Technical, Researcher, Trader, Risk Manager) that outperforms neural and rule-based baselines on cumulative return, Sharpe, and drawdown; v0.2.0 adds Claude 4.x support.
findings.relevance_notes: George has completed 27 rounds of backtesting. TradingAgents is the natural next step: instead of backtesting pure rules, use a multi-agent LLM layer on top of the best strategies as a filter/confirmation layer. Could be Round 28.

findings.title: Continual Meta-Learning for LLM Agents
findings.summary: Framework that jointly evolves LLM agent policies and reusable behavioral skills through opportunistic updates and skill-driven adaptation, enabling continual improvement without catastrophic forgetting.
findings.relevance_notes: Relevant to George's self-improvement loop. Skill library concept (persistent, reusable behaviors) maps to George's skills/ folder and could inspire a structured skill-tracking system.

findings.title: From AI Assistant to AI Scientist: POISE — Autonomous Discovery of LLM-RL Algorithms
findings.summary: POISE maintains a genealogically linked archive connecting proposals, implementations, evaluations, and reflections to drive closed-loop autonomous algorithm discovery, improving AIME25 pass@32 from 26.7% to 43.3%.
findings.relevance_notes: Meta-level: George's dream cycle IS a POISE-style loop. Confirms the staged-change + reflect + evaluate architecture. Also relevant to the trading_eval harness — could apply POISE-style genealogy to track which strategy combinations led to better Sharpe.

findings.title: From LLM Reasoning to Autonomous AI Agents: A Comprehensive Review (v2)
findings.summary: Surveys ACP, MCP, and A2A agent communication protocols, with analysis of failure modes in multi-agent systems and future directions including dynamic tool integration via RL.
findings.relevance_notes: MCP protocol is already live in George's stack (NanoClaw MCP server). A2A and ACP are emerging — relevant for when George coordinates with external agents or services.

findings.title: Graph-theoretic Agreement Framework for Multi-agent LLM Systems
findings.summary: Formally models agreement dynamics in multi-agent LLM systems using graph theory, identifying conditions for consensus failure and mitigating error cascades.
findings.relevance_notes: Tangentially relevant to George's swarm tasks. Less critical than memory and trading papers.

findings.title: Generalist Agent with Memory-Based RL (UCL)
findings.summary: A generalist LLM agent that autonomously designs and improves task-specific agents through memory-based RL with stateful prompts and skill libraries.
findings.relevance_notes: Supports George's approach of maintaining stateful MEMORY.md with task-specific sub-agents. Skill library concept is relevant to the daily podcast, trading, and portfolio sub-agents.

findings.title: ROMA: Recursive Open Meta-Agent Framework
findings.summary: Breaks long-horizon tasks into subtask trees executed in parallel across agents, solving context window limitations without complex handoffs.
findings.relevance_notes: Relevant to George's team tasks — when launching swarms, a recursive task tree (ROMA-style) could prevent context overflow on long trading research runs.

findings.title: DyTopo: Dynamic Topology Routing for Multi-Agent Reasoning
findings.summary: Dynamically rewires agent-to-agent connections at each reasoning round via semantic matching, studying emergent group behavior among 70K+ autonomous LLM agents.
findings.relevance_notes: Research-level, not immediately applicable. Interesting for future swarm designs.

findings.title: From Spark to Fire: Error Cascade Mitigation in Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
findings.summary: Models how errors propagate across agent chains and proposes mitigation strategies including intermediate validation checkpoints.
findings.relevance_notes: Relevant for George's swarm tasks. Adding validation checkpoints between sub-agent handoffs could prevent silent failures like the podcast parser issue from March 14.
